This page lists the spec and status fields of Job and JobRun, each with its type, its limits and its description. The [Platform page](../../../platform/workloads/job.md) explains the concept, and the `metadata` of every kind is [the same](../../common-definitions.md#objectmeta).

## Job

::include[../../../../../api/types/v1alpha1/examples/job/job.yaml#job]

| apiVersion | kind |
| --- | --- |
| `funcd.io/v1alpha1` | `Job` |

### `Job.spec`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approval` | object, [`Job.spec.approval`](#jobspecapproval) | Whether a run waits for a person's approval of its preview before it runs. Unset, every run previews and waits. |
| `bindings` | object, [`Job.spec.bindings`](#jobspecbindings) | What the code may use: KV tables, Bucket prefixes, SQL databases, Lakes and Functions, each under an alias, and ConfigMaps and Secrets. A binding is the grant: a call on an alias with no binding is refused with 403. Each store, Lake, ConfigMap and Secret it names must be declared at the root, in this spec's kv, buckets, sql, lakes, configMaps or secrets. |
| `buckets` | array of [`Job.spec.buckets[]`](#jobspecbuckets) | The Buckets the Job declares: by name it creates and owns one, and a Bucket of that name that it does not own holds it in Pending with StoreNotOwned; by ref it uses an existing one. spec.bindings.blob binds only a declared Bucket. |
| `concurrency` | integer, 1 to 15 | How many of the Job's runs may hold a worker at once, those Previewing included: 1 to 15; unset means 1, and a local volume allows only 1. A run past it waits in Pending with Queued. |
| `configMaps` | array of [`Job.spec.configMaps[]`](#jobspecconfigmaps) | The ConfigMaps the Job declares: by name it defines one from its data, which goes with the Job, by ref it uses an existing one. spec.bindings.config binds only a declared ConfigMap. |
| `handler` | string, matching `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$` | The name of the export that the shim calls once for each run, such as handle. A Job without one, or whose code has no such export, is not Ready, with ShapeInvalid. |
| `image` | string | The OCI reference of the code's artifact: a registry reference with a tag or a digest, or an oci-layout:// reference to a layout on the server's disk. A Job whose image is missing, or cannot be resolved or pulled, starts no run. |
| `imageDigest` | string, a sha256 digest | The sha256 digest that funcd pulls the image by and checks it against. Unset, funcd resolves the image to its digest when it creates the Revision of a new spec and keeps that digest, so a tag that moves later changes nothing. |
| `kv` | array of [`Job.spec.kv[]`](#jobspeckv) | The KVStores the Job declares: by name it creates and owns one, and a store of that name that it does not own holds it in Pending with StoreNotOwned; by ref it uses an existing one. spec.bindings.kv binds only a declared store. |
| `lakes` | array of [`Job.spec.lakes[]`](#jobspeclakes) | The Lakes the Job declares: by name it creates one that goes with the Job, by ref it uses an existing one. spec.bindings.lake binds only a declared Lake, and a Lake declared by name declares nothing at its own root: it binds the Job's buckets, configMaps and secrets. |
| `resources` | object, [`Job.spec.resources`](#jobspecresources) | The CPU and memory caps of each run's worker; a field left empty takes functions.defaultResources. Only the containerd runtime enforces them. |
| `runtime` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The runtime that runs the code, such as nodejs22 or python314. A Job without one is not Ready, with ShapeInvalid, and one whose runtime this node cannot run is not Ready, with RuntimeUnavailable. |
| `secrets` | array of [`Job.spec.secrets[]`](#jobspecsecrets) | The Secrets of the namespace that the bindings may name, each with the keys the code reads; spec.bindings.secret names only a declared Secret. The Job waits in Pending, with SecretNotFound or SecretKeyMissing, until each one exists with every declared key. |
| `sql` | array of [`Job.spec.sql[]`](#jobspecsql) | The SQLDatabases the Job declares: by name it creates and owns one, and a database of that name that it does not own holds it in Pending with StoreNotOwned; by ref it uses an existing one. spec.bindings.sql binds only a declared database. |
| `timeout` | string, a duration: whole numbers with the units h, m, s and ms, largest unit first (10m, 1h30m, 500ms) | The bound on each call of a run's handler, its preview's and its apply's, from its worker's start: 0s to 168h; 0s or unset means none. A run past it ends Failed with RunTimedOut, and its worker stops. |
| `volumes` | array of [`Job.spec.volumes[]`](#jobspecvolumes) | The directories each run's worker mounts. Apply refuses a Job with one unless runtime.mode is containerd and volumes.capacity or volumes.capacityBytes is set. A local volume is the Job's own, never a same-named Function's, and allows a concurrency of at most 1. |

### `Job.spec.approval`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bypass` | boolean | When true, a run runs at once, with no preview and no approval. Unset or false, a run first calls the code's preview, then waits in AwaitingApproval until a person approves or rejects it. A Job for unattended work sets it. |
| `expiry` | string, a duration: whole numbers with the units h, m, s and ms, largest unit first (10m, 1h30m, 500ms) | How long a preview stays valid for its approval: 1m to 168h; unset means 24h. A preview older than this when it is approved, or when its run's slot frees after the approval, is previewed again: the run runs when the new preview is the same document, and waits for a new approval when it differs. |

### `Job.spec.bindings`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addon` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.addon[]`](#jobspecbindingsaddon) | The add-on objects whose engines the code calls, each under its alias: through ctx.addon.fetch, or with any HTTP client at FUNCD_ADDON\_&lt;ALIAS&gt;\_URL with the header X-Funcd-Addon-Token set to FUNCD_ADDON\_&lt;ALIAS&gt;\_TOKEN. Each call goes through funcd, which asks Cedar for addon::call and serves only the paths that the object's edge entry serves. |
| `blob` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.blob[]`](#jobspecbindingsblob) | The Bucket prefixes the code reaches through ctx.blob, and over S3 while the S3 gateway is on, each under its alias. The binding grants reads; only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names may write. A Bucket or prefix that does not exist yet holds the Function in Pending with BucketNotFound. |
| `config` | array of string values, each a DNS-1123 label | ConfigMaps whose keys each worker gets as environment variables when it starts, a later ConfigMap's value winning for a key that both hold. A key that starts with FUNCD\_, or that a bound Secret holds, is left out; and while the S3 gateway is on, a Function that binds a Bucket gets the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY that funcd issues it, in place of a ConfigMap's. A missing ConfigMap holds the Function Failed with ConfigResolveFailed. |
| `job` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.job[]`](#jobspecbindingsjob) | The Jobs whose runs the code starts with ctx.job.start and reads with ctx.job.get, each under its alias. The binding grants both, and a namespace Policy that forbids job::start or job::read to the Function revokes one. A run that the code starts passes the checks of a run that a person starts, and a Job's own spec refuses this list. |
| `kv` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.kv[]`](#jobspecbindingskv) | The KV tables the code reaches through ctx.kv, each under its alias. The binding grants reads; only the table's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names may write. A store or table that does not exist yet holds the Function in Pending with KVStoreNotFound. |
| `lake` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.lake[]`](#jobspecbindingslake) | The Lakes the code queries, each under its alias. The Function waits in Pending with LakeNotReady until every bound Lake is Ready. |
| `links` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.links[]`](#jobspecbindingslinks) | The Functions the code calls, each under its alias: through ctx.invoke one whose protocol is cloudevent, through ctx.fetch one whose protocol is http. Each target must exist in the namespace when this Function is applied, the namespace's links form no cycle, and a Function that a link targets cannot be deleted until the link goes. |
| `secret` | array of string values, each a DNS-1123 label | Secrets whose keys the code reads through ctx.secret, on each read and with no cache, a later Secret's value winning for a key that both hold. No value reaches the worker's environment. No worker starts while a bound Secret is missing, and a worker whose Function a Policy forbids to read one is not ready. |
| `sql` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.sql[]`](#jobspecbindingssql) | The SQLDatabases the code queries through ctx.sql, each under its alias. The binding grants reads; only the database's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names may write. A database that does not exist yet holds the Function in Pending with SQLDatabaseNotFound. |

### `Job.spec.buckets[].prefixes[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The prefix's name, unique within the Bucket. Over S3, it is the first segment of each object's key. |
| `owner` | object, [`Job.spec.buckets[].prefixes[].owner`](#jobspecbucketsprefixesowner) | The one Function, Lake or Job that may write the prefix, named with its kind, besides the writers that a RolesAssignment names. In a Bucket that a Function, a Lake or a Job declares by name, an omitted owner is that workload. In a Workflow's buckets, a Function owner names a step and a Lake owner a lake that the Workflow declares. The prefix that a Site serves its bundle from must have no owner, since the Site writes its builds there; the prefixes of a Site's ingress rules may have one. |
| `quota` | object, [`Job.spec.buckets[].prefixes[].quota`](#jobspecbucketsprefixesquota) | A cap on the prefix's total size: a write into the prefix must fit both this cap and the Bucket's, and while it is set funcd refuses to sign a presigned PUT URL into the prefix, with 403. ### `Job.spec.configMaps[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | map of string to string | Keys and their string values, for settings that are not secret. Each key is an environment variable name: ASCII letters, digits and \_, not starting with a digit. Each value must be UTF-8 text with no NUL byte: a Function or a Lake that binds a ConfigMap holding another value does not start. Each worker of a Function that lists the ConfigMap in bindings.config gets each key as an environment variable when it starts, except a key that starts with FUNCD\_ or that a bound Secret also holds; and while the S3 gateway is on, a Function that binds a Bucket gets the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY that funcd issues it, in place of the ConfigMap's. A Lake that lists it gives its engine only the keys that the Lake's bindings.config lets through. |
| `name` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The ConfigMap's name, at most 52 characters. It is stored as &lt;name&gt;-&lt;hash of data&gt;, and the config of each part that names it is set to that stored name. |
| `ref` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The name of an existing object of this kind in the namespace of the resource that declares it. A ref entry sets no other field. |

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxBytes` | integer, at least 0 | The same cap as a number of bytes. Set maxSize or maxBytes, not both. |
| `maxKeyBytes` | integer, 0 to 64000 | The longest key, in bytes. 0 means 1024 (1 KiB). |

### `Job.spec.kv[].tables[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The table's name, unique within the store. |
| `owner` | object, [`Job.spec.buckets[].prefixes[].owner`](#jobspecbucketsprefixesowner) | The Function or Job that owns the table, in the store's namespace, named with its kind. The owner writes the table, and so does a principal that a RolesAssignment grants kv::write on the table, its store or its namespace, such as the KV Data Writer role. In a store that a Function or a Job declares, the owner defaults to that workload; in one that a Workflow declares, a Function owner names a step, and the Function that funcd creates for that step is the owner; in a KVStore applied on its own, a table with no owner is written only through such a grant. Every workload, the owner included, reaches the table through an entry of its spec.bindings.kv. |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `blob` | array of [`Job.spec.bindings.blob[]`](#jobspecbindingsblob), required | The Bucket prefixes the engine may read, each under an alias. It writes only a prefix whose owner is this Lake, and the Lake's location must be one of them. |

A changed value replaces the engine. |

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string, one of `""`, `authenticated`, `open`, `oidc` | How the edge checks callers. authenticated requires a bearer token, or an X-Api-Key header, of an identity that RBAC lets get Functions in the namespace: 401 without a valid one, 403 when it may not; while server.auth.edge is off, every caller gets 401. open lets anonymous callers in. oidc signs callers in with the OIDCProvider that provider names, and passes the signed-in user to the code behind it in the X-Funcd-Principal headers. Empty takes the enclosing stance, if any, else the namespace's spec.edgeDefaults.auth.mode, else open. |
| `provider` | string, a DNS-1123 label | With mode oidc, the OIDCProvider of the namespace that signs callers in; required with oidc and refused with another mode. |
| `unauthenticated` | string, one of `""`, `redirect`, `401`, `allow` | With mode oidc, what a call that is not signed in gets: redirect, the default, sends a GET or HEAD navigation to the provider with 302 and gives any other call 401; 401 gives every such call 401; allow passes every call, with no principal. Refused with another mode. |

### `Job.spec.lakes[].location`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bucket` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | A Bucket of the same namespace. |
| `prefix` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | A prefix of that Bucket. |

### `Job.spec.lakes[].secrets[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | What the Secret is for, for the installer who provides it. |
| `keys` | array of string values, required, each matching `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` | The keys read from the Secret: its data must hold each of them. |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The name of a Secret in the namespace of the resource that declares it. funcd holds its value; the resource never writes it. |

### `Job.spec.resources`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpu` | string | The CPU cap of the worker or engine it sizes, as a number of cores of at least 0.01, such as 0.5 or 2. Empty takes the default of the resource that declares it, or no cap when there is none. Only the containerd runtime enforces it. |
| `memory` | string | The memory cap of the worker or engine it sizes, such as 256Mi or 4GiB: 1 to 15 digits and an optional binary unit, Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti, with or without a B, above zero. Empty takes the default of the resource that declares it, or no cap when there is none. Only the containerd runtime enforces it, and there a worker that uses more memory than the cap is killed. |

### `Job.spec.secrets[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | What the Secret is for, for the installer who provides it. |
| `keys` | array of string values, required, each matching `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` | The keys read from the Secret: its data must hold each of them. |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The name of a Secret in the namespace of the resource that declares it. funcd holds its value; the resource never writes it. |

### `Job.spec.sql[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deletion` | string, one of `retain`, `delete` | retain (the default) keeps the store and its data when the resource that declares it is deleted, and delete removes them. An App applies the same choice when it drops the entry. |
| `name` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The object's name. It takes the namespace and resource group of the resource that declares it. |
| `owner` | object, [`Job.spec.buckets[].prefixes[].owner`](#jobspecbucketsprefixesowner) | The one Function, Lake or Job that may write the database, in its namespace, named with its kind, besides the writers that a RolesAssignment names. In a database that a Function or a Job declares by name, it defaults to that workload, and in a Workflow's sql a Function owner names a step and a Lake owner a lake that the Workflow declares. A Lake writes no SQL, so a database a Lake owns is written by those writers only. With no owner, only those writers can write it. |
| `quota` | object, [`Job.spec.buckets[].prefixes[].quota`](#jobspecbucketsprefixesquota) | A cap on the database's total size, the bytes of its pages in use. Once it is reached, an execute gets 507 unless each of its statements is a DELETE or a DROP. A change keeps the engine running. |
| `ref` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The name of an existing object of this kind in the namespace of the resource that declares it. A ref entry sets no other field. |
| `resources` | object, [`Job.spec.resources`](#jobspecresources) | The cpu and memory of the database's engine. An empty memory means 256Mi, and an empty cpu sets no cpu limit. A change replaces the running engine. |

### `Job.spec.volumes[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deletion` | string, one of `retain`, `delete` | Only for a local volume declared by name: retain, the default, keeps the volume and its files with no owner when the Function drops it or is deleted, so that a ref can take it again; delete removes them. |
| `name` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The volume's name, unique in the list; set name or ref, not both. The code reads the directory's path from FUNCD_VOLUME\_&lt;NAME&gt;, the name or ref upper-cased. |
| `ref` | string, a DNS-1123 label | Instead of name: a retained local volume that this Function, or an earlier Function of the same name, dropped with retain, and that the Function takes over; with no such volume, it waits in Pending with VolumeNotFound. Only a local volume takes a ref; it sets no deletion and states the retained volume's own size, since apply refuses another size. |
| `size` | string, a size: 1 to 15 digits and an optional binary unit, Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti, with or without a B (512Ki, 2GiB) | The volume's size, the most its directory may hold, above zero; set size or sizeBytes, not both. Apply refuses a local volume whose size changes, or that does not fit both the capacity that volumes.capacity or volumes.capacityBytes sets and the namespace's spec.volumeBudget. |
| `sizeBytes` | integer, at least 1 | The same size as a number of bytes. Set size or sizeBytes, not both. |
| `type` | string, required, one of `emptyDir`, `local` | emptyDir is a new empty directory for each worker, removed with it; local is one durable directory that keeps its files through a crash, a redeploy and a scale to zero. A Function with a local volume runs at most 1 replica, and while it redeploys, its old and new workers hold the volume at once. |

| `currentRevision` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The Revision of the latest spec, named &lt;job&gt;-v&lt;generation&gt;. A run pins the current one when it starts, and keeps it until it ends. |

| --- | --- | --- |

## JobRun

::include[../../../../../api/types/v1alpha1/examples/job/jobrun.yaml#jobrun]

| apiVersion | kind |
| --- | --- |
| `funcd.io/v1alpha1` | `JobRun` |

### `JobRun.spec`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approve` | string, a sha256 digest | The digest of the preview that a person approves, status.preview.digest. A create that sets it is refused. An update that sets or changes it, or that keeps one with no recorded approval of the run's current preview, is taken only while the run is AwaitingApproval and the digest is the run's preview's, else it is refused with 409, and only from a caller who may update the run's Job, else with 403; an update that cancels or rejects the run is taken whatever it holds. It is never cleared. funcdctl job approve sets it. |
| `cancel` | boolean | When true, the run is cancelled: a run that has not started ends Cancelled, and a running one has its worker stopped first, though its handler may have done part of its work. It may only turn true, and a run that has ended ignores it. funcdctl job cancel sets it. |
| `input` | any JSON value | The run input, the data of the event that the handler receives. Over job.payloadLimit bytes, or off the input schema in the Job's status.contract, it is refused when the run is created. It is fixed once the run is created. |
| `job` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The Job to run, in the run's namespace, fixed once the run is created. The run waits in Pending while that Job is missing or not Ready. |
| `reject` | boolean | When true, the run ends Rejected and its handler never runs. A create that sets it is refused. An update may turn it true only while the run is Pending, Previewing or AwaitingApproval, and only from a caller who may update the run's Job; it may not turn false again. A rejection wins over an approval that funcd has not acted on yet. funcdctl job reject sets it. |
| `rejectReason` | string, 0 to 512 characters | Why the run is rejected: the message of its Ready condition once it ends Rejected, at most 512 bytes, which a text of more than one byte per character reaches before 512 characters. It is set with spec.reject, and a create that sets it is refused. |

### `JobRun.status`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approvedAt` | string, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp with exactly 3 fractional digits (2026-10-07T20:03:35.965Z) | When a person approved the run's preview. funcd runs a run only on an approval it recorded. |
| `approvedBy` | string | The subject of the credential that approved the run, which funcd sets with approvedAt; empty with none. A preview made again with another document clears both. |
| `conditions` | array of [Condition](../../common-definitions.md#condition) | The conditions that explain the phase. |
| `endedAt` | string, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp with exactly 3 fractional digits (2026-10-07T20:03:35.965Z) | When the run ended. |
| `imageDigest` | string | The digest of the image of the pinned Revision. |
| `jobRevision` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The Revision of the Job that the run runs, pinned when it starts: an edit of the Job during the run changes nothing for it. |
| `jobUID` | string | The UID of the run's Job, set when the run is created if the Job exists, else when it starts. A run whose Job is deleted, or re-created under a new UID, is cancelled. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | The generation of the spec that funcd last acted on. |
| `phase` | string, one of `Pending`, `Previewing`, `AwaitingApproval`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Rejected` | Where the run is: Pending while it waits for its Job or for a free slot, Previewing while its worker answers the code's preview, AwaitingApproval while it waits for a person to approve or reject that preview, and Running while its worker runs the handler. Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled and Rejected are final, and the Ready condition gives the reason. |
| `preview` | object, [`JobRun.status.preview`](#jobrunstatuspreview) | The answer of the code's preview, which a person approves by its digest. Empty for a run of a Job with approval.bypass. |
| `rejectedBy` | string | The subject of the credential that rejected the run, which funcd sets; empty with none. |
| `result` | any JSON value | The handler's answer, once the run Succeeded. |
| `startedAt` | string, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp with exactly 3 fractional digits (2026-10-07T20:03:35.965Z) | When the run started running. |
| `startedBy` | string | The subject of the credential that created the run, which funcd sets; empty when there was none. It records who started the run and grants nothing. |
| `traceId` | string | The run's W3C trace ID, 32 lowercase hex characters, the same for its preview and its run. funcdctl job logs reads the run's logs by it. |

### `JobRun.status.preview`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `digest` | string, required | sha256: and the hex digest of the preview's bytes, which spec.approve names. |
| `document` | any JSON value, required | The JSON document that the preview answered, or the run's input when the code has no preview. |
| `previewedAt` | string, required, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp with exactly 3 fractional digits (2026-10-07T20:03:35.965Z) | When the preview answered. A preview older than its Job's approval.expiry is previewed again when it is approved, or when its run's slot frees after the approval. |

## Handler API

The methods a handler calls on its context's clients, in each language funcd ships a shim for.

### `ctx`

#### TypeScript

The per-invocation context the shim passes to the handler.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `log(...args: unknown[]): void` | Writes the arguments as one log line at level INFO, as console.log does. |
| `invoke<I = unknown, O = unknown>(alias: string, input: I): Promise<O>` | Calls the function that the link named alias targets, and returns its result parsed from JSON, or null when it returns nothing. The target's event.data is input, except that an object with a top-level `data` or `specversion` key is taken as the whole CloudEvent, so event.data is only its `data`: send such an object inside an envelope, as `{ specversion: '1.0', data: { data: [1], page: 2 } }`. The link's timeout, 30 seconds by default, bounds the call. Fails with the HTTP status 403 when the function declares no link named alias, 409 when the target serves HTTP, 422 when input does not match the target's contract, and the target's status when its handler fails, such as 500. |
| `fetch(alias: string, path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>` | Sends an HTTP request to the function that the link named alias targets, which serves HTTP, and returns its reply as a Response, whatever its status. path starts with "/" and may carry a query; init sets the method, the headers and the body, as for the global fetch. The request body and the reply are each at most 1 MiB, and the link's timeout, 30 seconds by default, bounds the call. Fails with the HTTP status 403 when the function declares no link named alias, and 409 when the target does not serve HTTP. |
| `remainingMs(): number \| null` | The whole milliseconds left before the call's deadline, 0 once it has passed, or null when the call has none. |

Each method here that calls funcd can also fail with the status 500 and the problem type `urn:funcd:problem:internal`, when funcd meets an error that it did not expect; funcd logs its cause.

When funcd refuses a call, the method fails with an error that holds funcd's status and problem type. This table gives them for each method, with when each happens and what to do.

| Method | Status | Problem type | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | The Function's spec.bindings.links has no entry for the alias. | Add the link to spec.bindings.links, or call an alias that the Function links. |
| `invoke` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | A Policy forbids the Function to call the link's target. | Change or remove the Policy that forbids link::invoke on the target. |
| `invoke` | 404 | `urn:funcd:problem:not-found` | The Function that the link targets no longer exists, as when its App deleted it before the Function that links it. | Create the Function again, or link one that exists. |
| `invoke` | 409 | `urn:funcd:problem:conflict` | The link's target serves HTTP, which ctx.invoke does not call. | Call it with ctx.fetch, which only the TypeScript shim has, or link a Function whose protocol is cloudevent. |
| `invoke` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The request's body is larger than the local API takes for the call. | Send a smaller body. |
| `invoke` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The target's reply is larger than 1 MiB, the most that a call carries back. | Return a smaller reply, or pass the data through a Bucket. |
| `invoke` | 429 | `urn:funcd:problem:resource-exhausted` | The target already has as many calls from Functions in flight as invoke.maxNestedInFlight allows. | Retry once a call to the target returns, or raise invoke.maxNestedInFlight. |
| `invoke` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The target's reply broke off before its end: its worker failed during the call, or the link's timeout ended it. | Retry the call, and raise the link's timeout if the target needs longer. |
| `fetch` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | The Function's spec.bindings.links has no entry for the alias. | Add the link to spec.bindings.links, or call an alias that the Function links. |
| `fetch` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | A Policy forbids the Function to call the link's target. | Change or remove the Policy that forbids link::invoke on the target. |
| `fetch` | 404 | `urn:funcd:problem:not-found` | The path names no alias: it is not /fetch/&lt;alias&gt;/&lt;path&gt;. | Pass the alias of a link, and a path that starts with /. |
| `fetch` | 404 | `urn:funcd:problem:not-found` | The Function that the link targets no longer exists, as when its App deleted it before the Function that links it. | Create the Function again, or link one that exists. |
| `fetch` | 409 | `urn:funcd:problem:conflict` | The link's target does not serve HTTP, which ctx.fetch needs. | Call it with ctx.invoke, or link a Function whose protocol is http. |
| `fetch` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The request's body is larger than the local API takes for the call. | Send a smaller body. |
| `fetch` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The target's reply is larger than 1 MiB, the most that a call carries back. | Return a smaller reply, or pass the data through a Bucket. |
| `fetch` | 429 | `urn:funcd:problem:resource-exhausted` | The target already has as many calls from Functions in flight as invoke.maxNestedInFlight allows. | Retry once a call to the target returns, or raise invoke.maxNestedInFlight. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The target's reply broke off before its end: its worker failed during the call, or the link's timeout ended it. | Retry the call, and raise the link's timeout if the target needs longer. |

#### Python

The per-invocation context the shim passes to the handler.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `log(*args: object) -> None` | Prints the arguments, separated by spaces, as one line on standard output, which funcd keeps as a log line at level INFO. |
| `invoke(alias: str, payload: Any) -> Any` | Calls the function that the link named ``alias`` targets, and returns its result parsed from JSON, or ``None`` when it returns nothing. The target's ``event["data"]`` is ``payload``, except that a dict with a top-level ``"data"`` or ``"specversion"`` key is taken as the whole CloudEvent, so ``event["data"]`` is only its ``"data"`` value: send such a dict inside an envelope, as ``{"specversion": "1.0", "data": payload}``. The link's timeout, 30 seconds by default, bounds the call. Fails with the HTTP status 403 when the function declares no link named ``alias``, 409 when the target serves HTTP, 422 when ``payload`` does not match the target's contract, and the target's status when its handler fails, such as 500. |
| `remaining_ms() -> int \| None` | The whole milliseconds left before the call's deadline, 0 once it has passed, or ``None`` when the call has none. |

Each method here that calls funcd can also fail with the status 500 and the problem type `urn:funcd:problem:internal`, when funcd meets an error that it did not expect; funcd logs its cause.

When funcd refuses a call, the method fails with an error that holds funcd's status and problem type. This table gives them for each method, with when each happens and what to do.

| Method | Status | Problem type | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | The Function's spec.bindings.links has no entry for the alias. | Add the link to spec.bindings.links, or call an alias that the Function links. |
| `invoke` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | A Policy forbids the Function to call the link's target. | Change or remove the Policy that forbids link::invoke on the target. |
| `invoke` | 404 | `urn:funcd:problem:not-found` | The Function that the link targets no longer exists, as when its App deleted it before the Function that links it. | Create the Function again, or link one that exists. |
| `invoke` | 409 | `urn:funcd:problem:conflict` | The link's target serves HTTP, which ctx.invoke does not call. | Call it with ctx.fetch, which only the TypeScript shim has, or link a Function whose protocol is cloudevent. |
| `invoke` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The request's body is larger than the local API takes for the call. | Send a smaller body. |
| `invoke` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The target's reply is larger than 1 MiB, the most that a call carries back. | Return a smaller reply, or pass the data through a Bucket. |
| `invoke` | 429 | `urn:funcd:problem:resource-exhausted` | The target already has as many calls from Functions in flight as invoke.maxNestedInFlight allows. | Retry once a call to the target returns, or raise invoke.maxNestedInFlight. |
| `invoke` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The target's reply broke off before its end: its worker failed during the call, or the link's timeout ended it. | Retry the call, and raise the link's timeout if the target needs longer. |
